To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
decayless kink standing waves are driven by the energy flux from the photosphere and that their amplitudes are not a good measure of the energy flux.
Decayless kink oscillation amplitudes are not directly correlated with the input energy flux from different driving mechanisms.

1) The amplitudes of decayless kink standing oscillations are only weakly dependent on the input energy flux from the driver, 2) the line width energy flux estimates are not correlated to the input energy flux, and 3) the line width estimates are affected by the line-of-sight angle, and thus, a combined analysis of imaging data and spectroscopic data is needed for a reliable estimation of the energy flux.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy fluxes of decayless oscillations and the relation between them and their amplitudes.
the energy budget of decayless oscillations.
the energy input into the oscillations and its possible relation to the amplitudes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the energy fluxes of drivers for decayless oscillations cannot be estimated with the current available data, and the observed low amplitudes of decayless oscillations are not necessarily connected to low energy fluxes of their drivers.
decayless kink waves may be a possible candidate for coronal heating, but more work needs to be done in order to confirm this.
there is a strong correlation between the input driver energy fluxes and the amplitudes and line widths of the decayless kink waves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the energy fluxes of decayless kink loops are not necessarily low and that the energy transfer from the oscillations to the plasma may be significant, but it cannot be estimated from the amplitudes only.

the observed decayless oscillations are not necessarily associated to small energy fluxes, as the amplitudes do not show a clear correlation with the input energy flux from our synthetic data. Proc. SPIE 990

The main takeaway from our work is that
decayless kink waves are not necessarily low amplitude oscillations, but they can be associated with significant energy fluxes, which are comparable to the radiative losses of the quiet solar corona.

the amplitudes do not necessarily correlate with the input energy flux, and that the amplitutes of the decayless kink modes can be significantly lower than the ones observed in decaying oscillations, but the input energy flux can be of the same order of magnitude.
the observed amplitutes of the decayless coronal oscillations may correspond not only to weak drivers, as was thought so far.
